cite: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §16600(a)-(b) (as amended by SB 699, eff. Jan. 1, 2024)
proposition: §16600 voids agreements restraining engagement in a lawful profession/trade/business to that extent; read broadly, per Edwards, to void employment non-competes no matter how narrowly tailored, absent a statutory exception.

cite: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §16600.5(a)-(e) (SB 699, eff. Jan. 1, 2024)
proposition: Contracts void under the chapter are unenforceable and may not be enforced (or entered into) regardless of where and when signed and regardless of where the employment was maintained; attempts to enforce are civil violations; employees may sue for injunctive relief and actual damages, and a prevailing employee shall recover attorney's fees and costs.

cite: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §16600.1(a)-(c) (AB 1076, eff. Jan. 1, 2024)
proposition: Unlawful to include a noncompete clause not satisfying a chapter exception; individualized written notice that the clause is void was due to covered current and post-1/1/2022 former California employees by February 14, 2024 (last known address and email); a violation is an act of unfair competition under §17200.

cite: Cal. Lab. Code §925(a)-(e)
proposition: Employer may not require an employee who primarily resides and works in California, as a condition of employment, to adjudicate outside California a claim arising in California or to forfeit California's substantive protections; offending provisions are voidable by the employee, and if voided the matter is adjudicated in California under California law; discretionary employee fee award; exception only where the employee was in fact individually represented by counsel in negotiating forum/choice of law.

cite: Edwards v. Arthur Andersen LLP, 44 Cal.4th 937 (2008)
proposition: §16600 voids employment non-competes unless a statutory exception applies; the 'narrow restraint' exception is rejected; restraints are void even if narrowly drawn.

cite: Ixchel Pharma, LLC v. Biogen, Inc., 9 Cal.5th 1130 (2020)
proposition: Rule of reason applies to §16600 challenges in business-to-business contracts only; the employment context remains governed by Edwards and non-competes are void.

cite: Restatement (Second) of Conflict of Laws §187(2)
proposition: Chosen state's law is applied unless application would contravene a fundamental policy of a state with a materially greater interest in the issue whose law would govern absent an effective choice (or no substantial relationship).

cite: Nedlloyd Lines B.V. v. Superior Court, 3 Cal.4th 459 (1992)
proposition: California follows Restatement §187: choice of law enforced unless contrary to a fundamental policy of California where California has a materially greater interest in the issue.

cite: Application Group, Inc. v. Hunter Group, Inc., 61 Cal.App.4th 881 (1998)
proposition: California had a materially greater interest in applying §16600 to a non-compete of an out-of-state (Maryland) employer with a Maryland choice-of-law clause against an employee connected to California; California's policy against non-competes is fundamental and the foreign clause did not control.

cite: DeSantis v. Wackenhut Corp., 793 S.W.2d 670 (Tex. 1990)
proposition: Texas applies Restatement §187; a contractual choice of another state's law does not control non-compete enforceability where the state with the materially greater interest has a fundamental contrary policy (there, Florida law displaced as to a Texas employee).

A covenant not to compete is enforceable if ancillary to an otherwise enforceable agreement and reasonable as to time, geography, and scope of activity, restrained no more than necessary to protect goodwill/business interests; promisee bears the burden when the agreement's primary purpose is personal services; court must reform unreasonable limitations and enforce as reformed, but may not award damages for pre-reformation breach; §15.51 remedies are exclusive.

cite: Alex Sheshunoff Mgmt. Servs., L.P. v. Johnson, 209 S.W.3d 644 (Tex. 2006)
proposition: A non-compete in an at-will employment agreement is supported where the employer's promise (e.g., to provide confidential information) is performed, even if not at the moment of contracting, modifying Light v. Centel's timing requirement; core inquiry is reasonableness under §15.50.

cite: Marsh USA Inc. v. Cook, 354 S.W.3d 764 (Tex. 2011)
proposition: Stock-option consideration reasonably related to the employer's goodwill interest can support a covenant not to compete; rejects a narrow 'give rise' requirement for the consideration.

cite: Advanced Bionics Corp. v. Medtronic, Inc., 29 Cal.4th 697 (2002)
proposition: California courts should generally not enjoin a party from pursuing litigation in another state's courts in non-compete disputes; caution about interstate forum conflicts, without retreating from §16600 policy.

cite: Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code §17.042; Michiana Easy Livin' Country v. Holten, 168 S.W.3d 777 (Tex. 2005) (library practice note)
proposition: A forum-selection clause consenting to Travis County generally supplies consent to personal jurisdiction, but if voided under §925 the Texas court must find independent minimum contacts (two short business trips plus a Texas-employer contract may or may not suffice); a Texas injunction would face non-recognition in California on public-policy grounds for the non-compete.

cite: Campbell v. Board of Trustees, 817 F.2d 499 (9th Cir. 1987)
proposition: Applied a 'narrow restraint' exception under §16600; reasoning expressly rejected by the California Supreme Court in Edwards (2008) — not California law; flagged to the client as unavailable, not relied on.

cite: General Commercial Packaging, Inc. v. TPS Package Engineering, Inc., 126 F.3d 1131 (9th Cir. 1997)
proposition: Upheld a provision as a 'narrow restraint' outside §16600; disapproved in Edwards (2008); flagged as unusable, not relied on.

cite: FTC Non-Compete Clause Rule, 16 C.F.R. Part 910, 89 Fed. Reg. 38342 (May 7, 2024)
proposition: Would have banned most worker non-competes with notice duties; set aside nationwide in Ryan LLC v. FTC before ever taking effect; flagged as unusable, not relied on.

cite: Ryan LLC v. Federal Trade Commission, 739 F. Supp. 3d 496 (N.D. Tex. 2024)
proposition: FTC lacked substantive rulemaking authority under §6(g) and the Rule was arbitrary and capricious; Rule set aside nationwide under the APA; appeal voluntarily dismissed September 2025 — state law controls.

cite: Firm memo (2024): 'Enforcing Texas non-competes against remote California employees'
proposition: Internal background only, not legal authority: the firm previously recommended Travis County filings (Alvarez matter) on the strength of Calderon and Westbrook, which are NOT in the library and cannot be verified here; we do not rely on them.

cite: Firm memo (2025): 'Post-Ryan landscape'
proposition: Internal background only, not legal authority: with the FTC rule enjoined, state law controls; the 2024 position is 'pending further guidance' and notes en banc rehearing was granted in Westbrook (argued Jan. 2025) — its current status is unverified.
